current_date: June 2024 (cover title 'Hertfordshire County Council Local List for the Validation of Planning Applications (June 2024)'; the Validation Requirements section still calls it the '(January 2024)' list)
current_evidence: WebFetch was refused by the site (robots_disallowed). The council's Planning applications and decisions page says 'The validation checklist gives details about the supporting information which must accompany applications' and also refers to a 'Proposed validation checklist - please submit your comments', which suggests a revision is pending. No newer adopted list was found by search.

issues.detail: Grokbot turned exclusions into inclusions. It files 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' (L31) under Householder and Lawful development cert, which are the only two types the document excludes. It files 'Air Quality Assessment' (L1) under Householder although its trigger says '(excluding householders)'. The County Council does not determine householder applications at all. L31 is also missing from the types it does cover: Full planning, Outline, Reserved matters, Minerals & waste and County own development (Reg 3).
issues.evidence: L31 Sustainability Statement/Appraisal, When Required: 'All applications except householders, certificates of lawfulness.' Introduction: 'The County Council only deal with minerals and waste applications, and the County Council's own development, such as schools.'

issues.detail: The Minerals & waste (county) and County own devt (Reg 3) sheets are nearly empty: three rows and one row. About 30 rows were put under Full planning as 'INFERRED', yet many triggers name these types outright. The following are missing from Minerals & waste: Bird Strike Management Plan (L5: mineral extraction, landfill, sewage disposal), Transport Assessment (L32: 'All applications where the use of HGVs is required'), Statement of Community Engagement (L29: 'including minerals and waste and school proposals'), LVIA (L16: operational and restoration stages for minerals), Odour (L21) and Sustainability (L31). The following are missing from Reg 3: Travel Plan (L33: new or expanding schools), Statement of Community Engagement (school proposals), Mineral Resources Assessment (L19: 'Regulation 3 and waste applications'), Air Quality (L1: 'introduction of a new school ... close to an existing source of air pollution') and Playing Field Assessment (L24).
issues.evidence: L29: 'Major applications and where the development is expected to have significant effects on the local community including minerals and waste and school proposals.'; L33: 'For new schools or where schools will be expanding the number of pupils.'

issues.detail: The document applies its whole list to every 'planning application', which it defines as outline, full, reserved matters, s73 and s73A applications. Grokbot puts only Planning Statement and S106 Heads of Terms under Outline and Reserved matters, and marks Variation of condition s73 as having no local requirements. Heritage Statement (L13) is filed only under Listed building consent, although it also applies to any development affecting listed buildings, conservation areas, scheduled monuments, historic parks and gardens or World Heritage Sites. It is missing from Full planning, Minerals & waste and Reg 3.
issues.evidence: Types of Application: 'a planning application is an application for outline or full planning permission, for approval of reserved matters ..., an application pursuant to Section 73 ...'; L13: 'All applications for listed building consent and for developments affecting the historic environment'

issues.detail: L25 Restoration Strategy and Aftercare is missing. It is required where proposals involve disturbing the ground to extract minerals or dispose of waste. It covers phasing, progressive restoration, cross sections, final landform, a landscape scheme, an Agricultural Land Classification statement where agricultural land is affected, and at least 5 years of aftercare. Grokbot kept only one sentence from it ('and proposed Agricultural Land Classification is required.'), and reused that sentence as two unrelated rows.
issues.evidence: L25, When Required: 'Where proposals involve the disturbance of the ground for the extraction of minerals or waste disposal.'

issues.detail: L22 Phasing Plan is missing. It is required for all mineral extraction and landfill applications, and must show the phasing of extraction or waste cells (1 or 5 year phases), restoration and landscape management. Mineral extraction proposals also need a quarry development plan showing bench heights in metres AOD.
issues.evidence: L22, When Required: 'All applications for mineral extraction and landfill.'

issues.detail: L20 Noise and/or Vibration Statement is missing. It is required in three cases: new development that could create noise affecting noise-sensitive uses such as homes, hospitals and schools; noise-sensitive development next to an existing noisy use; and minerals and road developments, all land-filling and land-raising, reworking of former landfill sites and inert waste recycling where the proposal is likely to raise noise above background levels. Grokbot's 'Odour / Dust / Vibration assessment' row is named for vibration but carries only a dust cross-reference.
issues.evidence: L20, When Required: 'Minerals and road developments, all land-filling and land raising applications; reworking or reclamation of former landfill sites; recycling of inert waste ...'

issues.detail: L6 Borehole or Trial Pit Analysis is missing. It is required for all mineral extraction proposals and must give the depth and volume of soils and minerals to be extracted, the mineral type and the position of the winter water table.
issues.evidence: L6, When Required: 'For all mineral extraction proposals.'

issues.detail: L7 Climate Change Statement is missing. It is required for mineral extraction and waste proposals and must set out the measures considered to adapt to and mitigate future climate change impacts (Waste Core Strategy Policy 10).
issues.evidence: L7, When Required: 'For mineral extraction and waste proposals.'

issues.detail: L19 Mineral Resources Assessment is missing. It is required for Regulation 3 and waste applications on areas of significant mineral resources or within the County Council's Mineral Consultation Area. It must establish the extent, quality and viability of the resource so the Mineral Planning Authority can judge whether the mineral should be extracted first or may be sterilised.
issues.evidence: L19, When Required: 'Regulation 3 and waste applications on areas of significant mineral resources or within the County Council's Mineral Consultation Area'

issues.detail: L3 Bio-aerosol Assessment is missing. It is required for proposals that handle, store or treat biodegradable waste, particularly composting within 250 metres of sensitive land uses such as dwellings. Anaerobic digestion in an enclosed building must show that no bioaerosols will be generated.
issues.evidence: L3, When Required: 'Proposals involving the handling, storage or treatment of biodegradable wastes, particularly composting within 250 metres of sensitive land uses such as dwellings.'

issues.detail: L28 Soils Management and Handling Strategy is missing. It is required for mineral applications that involve significant development of agricultural land, and needs a detailed soil survey plus a plan for stripping, movement, storage and replacement. Grokbot's 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' row carries text from L25 (Restoration), not this requirement or its trigger.
issues.evidence: L28, When Required: 'For mineral applications where significant development of agricultural land is involved.'

issues.detail: L26 Rights of Way is missing. It is required where a public right of way crosses or passes close to the site, or where construction needs a temporary diversion or closure of part of a route. It must give a detailed justification for any diversion or closure.
issues.evidence: L26, When Required: 'Where a public right of way traverses or passes close by the application site or involves the temporary diversion or closure of part of a route'

issues.detail: L12 Geo-Diverse Assessment is missing. It is required for development that poses a risk to a designated site of geological or geomorphological importance, or to a notable geological or geomorphological feature within the site. It must show the alternatives considered, mitigation and monitoring.
issues.evidence: L12, When Required: 'Developments that pose a risk to a designated site of geological/geomorphological importance or a notable geological/geomorphological feature within the application site.'

issues.detail: The Green Belt Statement is missing. It is required for all applications in the Hertfordshire Green Belt, as part of the Planning Statement, and must set out very special circumstances where the proposal is contrary to Green Belt policy. Most mineral and waste sites in the county are in the Green Belt. Grokbot's Planning Statement excerpt stops before this sentence.
issues.evidence: L23 Planning Statement: 'All applications in the Hertfordshire Green Belt must provide a Green Belt Statement as part of the Planning Statement.'

issues.detail: The Surface Water Drainage Statement pro-forma (Appendix 1, LLFA template) is missing. It must be completed in full and submitted with every major application, covering impermeable areas, discharge route, peak rates, volumes, attenuation storage and SuDS maintenance. The L30 footnote also requires new FRAs and drainage strategies to use FEH22 rainfall data, and says FSR and FEH1999 data are not accepted.
issues.evidence: Appendix 1: 'this pro-forma must be completed in full and be submitted with any planning application which seeks permission for 'major' development'

issues.detail: The Travel Plan row (L33) carries the Transport Assessment trigger ('All applications where there is likely to be a significant impact upon the existing transport network, and/or where additional parking is proposed'). The real trigger is new schools, or schools increasing pupil numbers, and the plan must show how new pupils will reach the site by public transport or hired coaches.
issues.evidence: L33 Travel Plan, When Required: 'For new schools or where schools will be expanding the number of pupils.'

issues.detail: Several rows hold only the 'Why Required / Policy Drivers' preamble and stop before 'When Required', so no trigger is captured. Tree Survey (L34) should read 'trees within, on the boundary or in close proximity to the site that could be affected'. Surface Water Drainage Strategy (L30) should read 'Major applications and all development likely to significantly increase or change patterns of surface water run-off'. Daylight and Sunlight (L8) is cut at 'When Requi'. Site plan (N5: all applications), Sections and site levels (N11: all major applications), Elevations (N9: all except change of use or lawfulness certificates with no external changes, and s73) and Roof plans (N10: changes to roofs or new buildings, except s73) have the same problem.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt for Tree Survey ends '...British Standard BS5837:2012 'Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – recommendations.'

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut off and lose key clauses. Air Quality (L1) ends '...on air quality; a', dropping 'all minerals and waste applications' and the HGV traffic, permitted-emissions and new-school clauses. Flood Risk Assessment (L11) keeps only the first clause ('1 hectare or greater in Flood Zones 1, 2 and 3') and drops: operational development under 1 ha in Flood Zones 2 and 3; changes of use to highly or more vulnerable uses in Flood Zones 2 and 3; water-compatible to less vulnerable in Flood Zone 3; and culverting, or works within 20 m of a main river bank. Transport Assessment (L32) drops 'All applications where the use of HGVs is required will require a Transport Assessment', the main trigger for minerals and waste. Landscape Scheme (L17) drops 'Applications for full planning permission (apart from change of use) should be accompanied by a fully detailed scheme'. Land Contamination (L15) stops at 'former landfill sites, and', dropping 'former mineral tips' and the landfill gas risk assessment for sites on or within 250 m of a former landfill. BNG (L4), Design and Access Statement (N6) and Heritage Statement (L13) are also cut mid-word.
issues.evidence: L32: 'All applications where the use of HGVs is required will require a Transport Assessment (TA).'

issues.detail: Several triggers are fragments lifted from other parts of the document. Ecological Survey (L10) carries L4 Biodiversity 'What Information' text; its real trigger is 'Major applications and when proposals could result in a new loss to biodiversity, negatively affected protected habitats or species or priority habitats or species'. 'Odour / Dust / Vibration assessment' carries the L1 cross-reference 'please see 'Dust Assessment''; the L9 Dust Assessment trigger is 'developments with the potential to generate dust and applications involving major construction works where dust is likely to be an issue'. The lighting row carries L18 'What Information' text; its trigger is 'Planning applications involving exterior lighting or where exterior lighting will be required'. The Bird Strike row starts mid-sentence and drops 'mineral extraction or quarrying, landfill, sewage'. 'Sunlight to gardens' is just 'gardens or amenity space.'
issues.evidence: L9 Dust Assessment, When Required: 'For developments with the potential to generate dust and applications involving major construction works where dust is likely to be an issue.'

issues.detail: The Environmental Statement (EIA) row uses a sentence about copies as its trigger. The document says EIA content is outside the scope of the local list, so this is neither a local requirement nor a trigger.
issues.evidence: 'The content of EIA applications is not considered in detail in this document as this is covered by separate legislation.'

issues.detail: Many rows carry a generic requirement name that does not match the document's item. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is L18 Lighting Statement/Scheme. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' appears nowhere in the document; it reuses an L25 sentence. 'Ground investigation / Geotechnical / Basement Impact Assessment' is L14 Hydrological/Hydrogeological Assessment (dewatering or effects on the water table). 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' is L27 Site Waste Management Plan (construction waste estimates, waste carriers and re-use/recycling rates for Reg 3 schemes over 500 m2), not bin storage. 'Ventilation / Extraction details (odour)' is L21 Odour Assessment. 'Minerals / Waste specific statements (county matters)' is L5 Bird Strike Management Plan. 'Open space / play space assessment' is L24 Playing Field Assessment.
issues.evidence: L27 Site Waste Management Plan: 'Estimates of waste arising, recordings of waste managed, list of waste carriers, proportion of wastes re-used, recycled, disposed.'

issues.detail: The council tab_items hold only 8 entries: 4 drawing-standard fragments and 4 'Submission rules' lines. Of the document's 34 Part Two local requirements (L1-L34), only Odour Assessment appears in tab_items, and it is misfiled under 'Submission rules'. Across app_type_rows Grokbot captured about 24 of the 34 local requirements in some form, and 10 are missing entirely. 'Req. items 38' and 'Extraction level: Full (automated)' overstate the coverage.
issues.evidence: Document headings 'PART TWO: Local Validation Requirements' L1-L34; Grokbot tab_items sections 'Drawing / document standards' and 'Submission rules' only

issues.detail: Several items are boilerplate or fragments, not requirements. From tab_items: 'It would be appreciated if the scale of the plans and paper size is no larger than is required', 'Please submit files in PDF format and labelled appropriately', 'This authority only wishes to receive one paper copy...' and the EIA copies sentence. From app_type_rows: 'Pre-application advice' (described as 'strongly recommended', not a validation item); 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans', a clause from the Planning Statement content text ('masterplans or development briefs'); 'Photographs / Photomontages', from L16 ('may be required'); and 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal', which is not in the document.
issues.evidence: Pre-Application Advice: 'A pre-application discussion with a Planning Officer is strongly recommended'

issues.detail: Some items are recorded twice. L8 Daylight and Sunlight appears as both 'Daylight / Sunlight / Overshadowing Assessment' and 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space', the second being the tail of the same trigger. 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' and 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' share one L25 sentence. Odour Assessment appears both in tab_items and as a Ventilation/Extraction row. 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms' copies the Planning Statement trigger on all four sheets; the document asks for Heads of Terms only within the Planning Statement 'where relevant'.
issues.evidence: L8: '...including associated gardens or amenity space.'; L23: 'S106 Heads of Terms should be included where relevant.'

issues.detail: The list date 2025-02-01 comes from PDF metadata. The document's own title dates it June 2024, and the body still refers to the January 2024 list. On a June 2024 date the list is about 29 months old as at 2026-11-04, so 'Outdated (>2y)?' should read Yes, not No. The document itself says the list must be reviewed at least every two years.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'Hertfordshire County Council Local List for the Validation of Planning Applications (June 2024)'; 'The following Local List, which needs to be reviewed at least every two years'

issues.detail: The uploaded file has the same name as the linked file and is the June 2024 list, so the link points at the adopted document. That list is now past its own two-year review point, and the council page invites comments on a 'Proposed validation checklist', so a replacement may follow. The text also still cites the July 2021 NPPF and describes BNG in pre-commencement terms. Re-check for a newer adopted list.
issues.evidence: Council page: 'Proposed validation checklist - please submit your comments to spatial.planning@hertfordshire.gov.uk.'; document: 'NPPF (revised July 2021)'

summary: Grokbot's extraction for this county minerals and waste authority is poor. It missed 10 of the 34 local requirements, mostly the core minerals and waste items: Restoration Strategy and Aftercare, Phasing Plan, Noise/Vibration, Borehole/Trial Pit, Climate Change, Mineral Resources, Bio-aerosol, Soils Management, Rights of Way and Geo-diversity. It also missed the Green Belt Statement and the LLFA drainage pro-forma, and filed most of what it did capture under Full planning with preamble, cut-off or borrowed trigger text and wrong labels. It put the Sustainability Statement under the only two types that statement excludes (Householder and Lawful development certificates). Its list date, taken from PDF metadata (2025-02-01) instead of the document's June 2024, hides that the list is now over two years old.
